citation: Salvador, G.N. 2023. Ancistrus cirrhosus. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2023: e.T49830571A164512524. Accessed on 05 May 2026.

documentation.range: Ancistrus cirrhosus is distributed in the Paraná-Paraguay and Uruguay river basins, in southern Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay (Fisch-Muller 2003, Oyakawa and Menezes 2011, GBIF 2019, SpLink 2020). There are several old and uncertain records of the species in central Brazil and Bolivia, which are unreliable. Isbrücker (1980) designed a lectotype and six paralectotypes from Buenos Aires, but that procedure was not considered valid by Fisch-Muller (2003).
documentation.population: There are no data on population size and trends for this species, but it seems to be common on its distribution (ICMBio 2018). Further information on its population is unknown.
documentation.habitats: Ancistrus cirrhosus has a rheophilic character (Benedito-Cecílio et al. 1997), being associated with rapid water streams and rocky substrate. The species has a marked territorial behaviour (Almirón et al. 2000) and the females deposit their adhesive eggs under the rocks (Sabaj et al. 1999). It has a detritivorous diet (Oliveira et al. 2005).
documentation.threats: The main threat to the species in the Paraná River basin is the construction of dams for power generation, which alter the flow of the river, harming rheophilic species, such as Ancistrus cirrhosus (Benedito-Cecílio et al. 1997). The species is also used as ornamental fish. Despite such threats, the impacts do not seem to directly affect the population of Ancistrus cirrhosus to the point of putting it at risk of extinction.
documentation.measures: Studies on taxonomy and distribution are needed to resolve the uncertainties surrounding the species (ICMBio 2018).
documentation.use_trade: The species is used as ornamental fish.
documentation.rationale: Despite the little information available on this species, it has a wide range and no significant threats. Therefore, it is assessed as Least Concern.
